# FAQ {.unnumbered}

## Process

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionProcess">   <div class="accordion-item">     <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading1">       <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse1" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse1">         How much time should I spend on RSiP?       </button>     </h2>     <div id="processCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">       <div class="accordion-body"> The Research Skills in Psychology course in this program is worth 5 ECTS. This is equivalent to 140 hours of work for each student. It is very likely that you will need less time, since multiple students will be working on the same parts. At the same time, it is also likely that you will have weeks where you are spending less time on the project (e.g., during exam weeks, while waiting for feedback, etc.) and weeks where you are spending more time (e.g., right before a deadline). Therefore, it is important to be mindful of everyone's schedule in order to successfully complete this project.       </div>     </div>   </div>   <div class="accordion-item">     <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading2">       <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse2" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse2">         I heard from my friends that they are doing something differently. Why are we not expected to do it the same way?       </button>     </h2>     <div id="processCollapse2" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading2" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">       <div class="accordion-body">         A RSiP project, and generally any scientific project, does not have one way of being done. There are many valid, acceptable, and evidence-supported approaches that can be taken depending on both needs of the project and the supervisor's preferred way of working. If you believe something can be done better, I am very happy to learn about your idea and potentially integrate it!      </div>     </div>   </div>     <div class="accordion-item">     <h2 class="accordion-header" id="processHeading3">       <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#processCollapse3" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="processCollapse3"> What if my group wants to change a deadline? </button>     </h2>     <div id="processCollapse3" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="processHeading3" data-bs-parent="#accordionProcess">       <div class="accordion-body"> Some deadlines in the course are strict and unchangeable, since they are given by the course coordinator and not the supervisor. The other deadlines are dependent on agreement with supervisor. If your group collectively agrees on moving a date of a deadline, you can contact me with proposed alternatives. However, moving a deadline likely means we have to move a meeting, since they are structured around the completed work. <div>
    For that reason, please also include at least <b>two</b> separate dates and a time span of 3 hours per date (e.g., February 1 between 12:00 and 15:00) on which the group is available to have the meeting. </div>     </div>   </div> </div>
```

## Content

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionContent">   <div class="accordion-item">     <h2 class="accordion-header" id="contentHeading1">       <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#contentCollapse1" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="contentCollapse1">         How many references should we include in the report?       </button>     </h2>     <div id="contentCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="contentHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionContent">       <div class="accordion-body">         This is a very common question, and it is one that (unfortunately for you) does not have an answer. I have read theses that included anywhere from 25 to 100+. The number of references does <b>not</b> provide any indication for the quality of the written work. However, lack of references can lead to plagiarism, unsupported claims, weak arguments, and worse final evaluation. Therefore, always remember to provide references for <b>all</b> of the claims/arguments you make, even if it is something you consider general knowledge.       </div>     </div>   </div> </div>
```

## Special circumstances

```{=html}
<div class="accordion" id="accordionSpecial">   <div class="accordion-item">     <h2 class="accordion-header" id="specialHeading1">       <button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#specialCollapse1" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="specialCollapse1">         What if a group member is not  contributing,
communicating, and/or adhering to our agreements?   </button>     </h2>     <div id="specialCollapse1" class="accordion-collapse collapse" aria-labelledby="specialHeading1" data-bs-parent="#accordionSpecial">       <div class="accordion-body"> As you know, RSiP is a group project and you are (mostly) being graded as a group. Grading is based on the assumption that the group worked together, showcasing a joint effort of 4-6 people. <div>
If a member is clearly not contributing, it is important to <b> contact me </b> as soon as possible. The sooner you do so, the sooner the problem will be solved.<div>
The problems will be solved according to the step-by-step plan outlined in the syllabus. In short, if you notice someone is not contributing, the first order of business is to hold a group discussion with the member. After that, you should inform me about the situation and agreements you reached.
<div>
If the situation persists, we will organize a meeting in which I will be present to discuss this further and agree on next steps. Finally, if no improvement is noticed after that, the student may be excluded from the course.
</div>     </div>   </div> </div>
```
